newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chinese warships near the Kalayaan group in the Spratly Islands in the South China Sea have ignored a Philippine demand to leave, Defense Secretary Renato de Villa said yesterday. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Senator Juan Ponce Enrile, head of the ways and means committee, vowed to slash the annual tax exemption of 146,000 pesos which was approved by the House of Representatives on Wednesday. (INQUIRER)
- President Ramos yesterday proposed changes in the Labour Code to reduce government interference in settling disputes between management and workers' unions. (CHRONICLE)

- Singapore's Keppel Group, which matched the one billion-peso offer made by the Lippo Group of Indonesia, bagged majority ownership of Monte de Piedad and Savings Bank after prolonged negotiations with officials of the Philippine Central Bank and Philippine Deposit Insurance Corp late Wednesday. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Prices of petroleum products in Singapore continued to drop last month, making possible another round of oil price reductions for next week. (MALAYA/BULLETIN)

- The Philippinne Central Bank plans to go back to the United States for the offering of its $1.25-billion Yankee bond issue after the May 20 meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve Board. (BULLETIN/TIMES)
